commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[rl] Train Snowball on shell-tool tasks (#11921)

Snowball presets can now train on tasks whose tools run shell commands.
Two problems blocked this. SkyRL bound a task machine only per dataset,
so a dataset that mixes Linux tasks (`command_semantics: linux_process`)
with shell-simulator tasks loaded those rows without a machine and
failed validation. Training also stopped when the model escaped half of
a surrogate pair in a tool call, such as an emoji's `\ud83d`: vLLM's
Hermes parser serializes tool-call arguments with `ensure_ascii=False`,
so the assistant message carried a lone surrogate, and the tokenizer
raised `TypeError: TextEncodeInput must be Union[...]` while rendering
the next turn. The task worker treats a `TypeError` as a defect and
stops the run.

The loader now also reads `task_spec.task_machine_by_command_semantics`;
a per-dataset binding still takes precedence. The binding has no
default-config entry, so existing presets keep their native
configurations and control pins. The chat client replaces each lone
surrogate in tool-call arguments with U+FFFD, so the tool runs with that
character; response token IDs keep the escape that the model wrote.
Restoring the `\uXXXX` escape is not enough: vLLM decodes the arguments
before the chat template writes them, and the Snowball template writes
the decoded value with `tojson`, so the lone surrogate returns.

The new `train-medium-tools` preset trains for ten updates on a required
`--tasks` selection, with the 100-task EvalLite active set at step 0 and
the last update. It runs shell-simulator tasks on ShellSim without
network access and Linux tasks on a Daytona sandbox with 1 CPU, 2 GB of
memory and 10 GB of disk, and allows 16 model turns per task. Linux
sandboxes and image graders use the Daytona RL organization
(`DAYTONA_RL_API_KEY`), because they serve training rollouts. The Linux
tasks in the smoke selection start from one pinned `python` registry
image with no declarative build, so they need one snapshot there. The
optimizer state stays on the CPU, because a full-window trajectory needs
the GPU memory for the policy update. The preset saves no checkpoint or
export by default. `shell_tool_preset` in `rl_agentic_recipe.py` holds
the task settings, so another model entry can reuse them.

A three-update run on 164 forge tasks (90 shell-simulator, 74 Linux)
completed. EvalLite scored 0.58 at step 0 and 0.55 after update 3 on all
100 tasks, the mean reward per update stayed below 0.01, and 2 of the
1,536 training rollouts were masked: one for a Daytona reset while
creating a grading sandbox and one for a vLLM internal error. The same
run without surrogate handling stopped at update 2. The completed run
restored the `\uXXXX` escape instead of using U+FFFD, so it does not
show that a lone surrogate was handled, and the replacement has not run
on the cluster. With the Snowball tokenizer and chat template and vLLM's
argument-decoding step, a message with the restored escape fails with
the same `TypeError` and a message with U+FFFD renders.

Supersedes #11763.

---------

Reduce repeated SkyRL composition in the Snowball CLI and gate tests.
The
train-long coordinator test supplies successful preflight responses
during its
CLI cases and keeps native launch inspection. The preset sweep validates
its
11 launch documents in one native process. Publication retry and schema

cases reuse native composition when only the generated attempt ID

| Mixed native failure and retry | 22.3s | 14.3s |

| Gate schema timeout and subprocess errors | 17.7s | 10.8s |

The PR's CPU job passed 173 tests. It measured 27.2 seconds for the

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[levanter] Skip oversized tracker artifacts instead of raising (#11950)

An optional debug artifact must never raise into training. At Exp5
scale, the
22,524,781-byte gzipped train-step JAXPR exceeded the W&B artifact
limit, and
the size refusal surfaced as an error in the train loop.

Trackers now expose their artifact size limit as max_artifact_bytes,
with None
meaning no limit. Before any upload, WandbTracker.log_artifact and
BackgroundTracker.log_artifact compare the artifact size with that
limit. An
artifact over the limit logs one warning naming the artifact, its size,
and
the limit, and the uploader is not called. The raising validate_artifact
check
is removed; the limit pre-check replaces it. The upload path has no
try/except, so upload errors still raise. Trainer.write_artifact still
writes
the artifact file to the run's log directory. Artifacts under the limit
upload
as before.

---------

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
Grade fenced JSON answers and numeric answer fields (#11931)

Accept a Markdown code fence only when it encloses the complete JSON
reply. For number tasks, `JsonAnswer` accepts finite JSON numbers in the
`answer` field and preserves their original literals for exact numeric
grading. `JsonValueAnswer` uses the same fence rule. Extra prose,
multiple fences, booleans, nonfinite numbers, duplicate keys, and
numeric answers on text tasks remain submission failures.

A grading regression reproduces the reported fenced numeric reply. It
failed before the change and now receives reward 1.0. Further
regressions cover decimal rounding, underflow, and multiple fenced
answers.

Fixes #9758

commits.author: XiaoyuanWang111
commits.message:
[verifyit] Make the IFEval checks follow their instruction text (#10928)

verifyit's IFEval checks now follow their instruction text, with these
known limits. language:response_language stays an approximation: one
hint word is enough, so an English reply with "na" passes Swahili.
change_case:english_capital and change_case:english_lowercase look only
at letter case, although their prompts also ask for English. Word counts
undercount Chinese, Japanese and other scripts written without spaces,
such as Thai, and keywords:start_end fails a Chinese reply that starts
and ends with the same two-letter word. count:count_increment_word,
which no row of the rlvr1, mopd or rlvr2 blends uses, keeps main's rule
except for the keyword matching described below.

RLVR1 rows in the SkyRL environment stay graded by NVIDIA's checks
(verifiable-instructions f46a5ac, through grade_instruction_following),
so that reward does not change. With its verifyit_enabled option on,
which no config on main sets, the environment takes only
punctuation:no_comma, punctuation:punctuation_dot and
punctuation:punctuation_exclamation from verifyit, and all three change.
Evalchemy's IFEval and IFBench scorers are separate code. verifyit's
checks do grade curated tasks, which carry their own graders: they are
the deterministic gate before the GLM judge in the instruction-following
component of the Nemotron Ultra mopd, rlvr1 and rlvr2 blends, and the
whole reward of TaskTrove's IFEval source (46,391 rows). That component
still routes the checks in SEMANTIC_INSTRUCTION_CONSTRAINTS to the
judge. The TaskTrove rubric now describes the checks as they work, so
the next curation run reviews those rows again; recipe versions do not
change, because these tasks name the checks and do not bundle their
code. On the 19,135 verdicts below, the checks pass 53.3% against 59.2%
on main and change 3,097 verdicts. We have not run them on TaskTrove,
mopd or rlvr2 rows.

An audit ([#10316
comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316#issuecomment-6629419598))
collected 19,135 constraint verdicts on RLVR1 rows, on replies from two
models whose replies were not used to write the checks, and had two
blinded model reviewers label a stratified sample of 293 (kappa 0.94,
consensus on 285). Weighted, the consensus contradicts main's checks on
18.3%, NVIDIA's on 10.6% and this work as reviewed (f7a7c26) on 7.9%,
which is 10.4 points fewer than main (95% interval 8.8 to 11.8). Later
fixes were written after reading the labels, so this branch's 35 errors
of the 285, weighted 4.14%, are no independent estimate.

On main, a word is a run of ASCII letters, digits, apostrophes and
hyphens, and a sentence ends only at ".", "!" or "?" before whitespace.
A word is now a letter or digit followed by letters, digits and
combining marks of any script, with apostrophes inside it; a hyphen
separates words, as in NVIDIA's word count. A run of Han or kana letters
is one word, since one word per letter overcounts. In the checks that
compare words (count:count_unique, count:lowercase_counting,
copy:repeat_phrase, detectable_format:bigram_wrapping,
keywords:start_end, keywords:keyword_specific_position,
length_constraints:nth_paragraph_first_word and the first_word and
last_word checks), each Han or kana letter is one word. In those checks,
a number with separators, such as "1,000", "3.5" or "10:30", is one
word, and so are single letters joined by dots, such as "U.S.". A
sentence also ends at a line break, at an ellipsis and at the
sentence-final marks of other scripts, and a sentence or paragraph must
hold a word. A keyword next to an underscore or a Han or kana letter is
now found, and one that a combining mark follows is not.

These rules change (main's rule in parentheses where the new one does
not imply it):

- count:lowercase_counting: each lowercase word at most N times (at
least N lowercase words).
- letters:letter_counting: letters of every script (words).
- count:count_unique: no word twice, ignoring case and a trailing 's (at
least 5 distinct words, at least half of all words).
- keywords:word_once: at least once, since the prompt only says to
include it (exactly once).
- keywords:word_count_different_numbers: exactly N times (a stored
relation the prompt does not show).
- copy:repeat_phrase: exactly N copies, each with one word replaced,
never the first or last word (at least N unchanged copies).
- keywords:no_adjacent_consecutive: no adjacent words with consecutive
first letters, in either order, by code point, Han and kana excepted (no
word repeated next to itself).
- length_constraints:number_paragraphs, paragraphs:paragraphs: exactly
the asked number between *** dividers; a *** that opens bold italics,
after whitespace, an opening bracket or quote or a Han or kana letter,
divides nothing, and neither does a run of four or more asterisks (blank
lines).
- paragraphs:paragraphs2: exactly two blank-line paragraphs (two or
more).
- count:counting_composition: three paragraphs of exactly N sentences of
exactly M words (the first N sentences have at least M words).
- detectable_format:multiple_sections: a marker starts a line or a
sentence, and each section has text (any mention).
- detectable_format:number_bullet_lists: the divider "* * *" does not
count as a bullet.
- combination:two_responses: the separator is exactly six asterisks, and
a "." after a closing separator does not count as a response.
- detectable_content:postscript: text must follow the marker, and
Markdown markup may precede it.
- detectable_format:square_brackets: every word inside a [...] span, and
no span holds whitespace (any bracketed span).
- detectable_format:bigram_wrapping: every word in a <<...>> span of
two; a line or sentence with an odd number of words may end in a span of
one, and spans of one may not outnumber spans of two (one Markdown bold
word pair).
- detectable_format:sentence_hyphens: a sentence end that no hyphen
joins to the next sentence fails, whether whitespace, a dash other than
a hyphen or the next word directly follows it, as in "One.Two."; so does
any line break (each sentence's words joined by hyphens).
- punctuation:no_comma, punctuation:punctuation_exclamation: any
punctuation that Unicode names a comma or an exclamation mark (only ","
and "!").
- punctuation:punctuation_dot: also "…", the fullwidth and small full
stops "．" and "﹒" and the dot leaders "․" and "‥" (only "."); 。 and the
full stops of other scripts stay allowed, since the prompt shows "." and
calls it a dot.
- startend:quotation: double quotes only (single quotes too).
- startend:end_checker: the phrase in any case, with no word after it
(the literal end of the reply).
- keywords:start_end: nothing, not even punctuation, may follow the last
word.
- keywords:palindrome: a word of at least 3 letters and digits, 2 of
them different, or a run of up to 12 words with at least 7 letters and
digits, 3 of them different (a word of at least 3).
- detectable_format:constrained_response: the option may sit in Markdown
emphasis or double quotes.
- detectable_format:title, detectable_content:number_placeholders: the
span must hold a non-space character.
- detectable_format:number_highlighted_sections: a highlight must hold a
word and not start or end with whitespace.
- change_case:english_capital, change_case:english_lowercase: modifier
letters are skipped.
- first_word:first_word_answer, first_word:first_word_sent,
last_word:last_word_answer, last_word:last_word_sent,
keywords:keyword_specific_position,
length_constraints:nth_paragraph_first_word, keywords:start_end: a
trailing 's is ignored, and outside keywords:start_end a required word
is split into words by the same rule as the reply.
- language:response_language: hint words for Finnish, Polish and Swahili
(the share of non-ASCII characters), and Hindi hint words that end in a
vowel sign now match.

startend:end_checker ignores case, as NVIDIA's checks do, because 93 of
the 11,817 RLVR1 rows pair the end phrase with all-lowercase or
all-capital text; of the two labeled replies with the phrase in another
case, the reviewers failed one and split on the other.
keywords:no_adjacent_consecutive takes either order because the prompt
says "consecutive letters"; the reviewers passed one reply with a
descending pair and failed another.

RLOO runs on the RLVR1 rows ([#10320
comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10320#issuecomment-6629312441))
compare the SkyRL reward with earlier states of this work (fork branch
rlvr1-if-checks-b, up to 4dd4b96f4); they inform a later decision on the
RLVR1 reward, and their training does not test this change. All six
SkyRL-reward runs learned an exploit of copy:repeat_phrase or
detectable_format:bigram_wrapping, none of the six runs on the earlier
states did, and on held-out IFBench the runs on the earlier states show
no consistent gain over the SkyRL-reward runs (-8.3 to +7.3 points).
Four of the six on the earlier states drifted to those states' weak
spots: Chinese replies on count:count_unique (as did the SkyRL-reward
runs that drifted to Chinese), and multi-line replies on
detectable_format:sentence_hyphens and, in two of them,
first_word:first_word_sent. In steps 271-300 of those four, the #10316
audit's replacement grader, which reads these three checks as this
branch does, fails 1,621 verdicts that the earlier states pass. This
branch fails all 1,621 and passes every verdict that the earlier states
and that grader both pass. Four later RLOO runs (seeds 1 to 4) used this
branch at 1628af76b as the reward ([#10320
follow-up](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10320#issuecomment-6697204992)).

A fresh import takes about 30 ms more than on main, and every check
stays under 0.5 s on 100,000-character degenerate inputs; on main,
detectable_content:postscript and, after an opening code fence,
detectable_format:json_format take over 30 s on 100,000 newlines.

Part of #10320.

commits.message:
[eval] Correct canonical task grading and scoring (#10927)

Apply five of the grading corrections that #10828 tracks and main lacks:

- IFBench uses #10423's seven checker fixes, so `repeat:repeat_span`
reads word indices. #10423's eight regression cases pass in strict and
loose mode.
- CRUXEval keeps the two rules of facebookresearch/cruxeval's harness
that `main` still lacks after #11928 changed its answer extraction: an
output answer containing `f(<input>)` fails, and an input answer without
`f(` fails, both without running. On `main`, `assert f('a', 'b') ==
f('a', 'b')` passes the output task, because the test program recomputes
`f`, and the bare output `'ab'` passes the input task. An input answer
keeps the call after `assert f`, as the harness does, so `The call is
assert f('a', 'b') == 'ab'` no longer fails to compile. It keeps
#10970's choice of block, the first `[ANSWER]` block that holds a
candidate.
- OlympiadBench and the boxed-answer scorer of MATH500, AIME24 and
AIME25 compare a reference that math-verify parses into relations
without free symbols only with the same relations, each identical or
reversed. The one such reference in these tasks is OlympiadBench id
1122's `I_{e}(0)=\gamma I_{i}(0)`, where math-verify reads `I_{e}(0)`
and `I_{i}(0)` as function values and `\gamma` as a constant; no MATH500
or AIME reference parses this way, so their grades do not change.
Before, that reference scored 0 against itself and `x = x` matched it.
- GSM8K strict-match, which the GSM8K tasks report beside their primary
flexible-extract metric, uses the rules that #10808 added to the
Evalchemy GSM8K task. Main's canonical scorer applies them only to
flexible-extract. Now `#### 18.` matches 18 and, on the 29 of 1,319
questions that mention a percent or pass rate, `#### 0.25` matches a
reference of 25.
- HumanEval+ and MBPP+ give the whole test program 60 seconds,
evalplus's cap for a task, because 3 seconds failed valid reference
solutions on time alone. A program that never ends now fails after up to
61 seconds instead of 4. HumanEval keeps 3 seconds and CRUXEval 10.

The first version's two default changes, final-content response
selection for chat tasks and BOS for likelihood contexts, are held for a
separate pull request because, after #10957, they reach corpus
identities and the execution revision.

The table regrades reference solutions and the saved outputs of earlier
runs, which sent the requests of
`experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled` to
models served with its configs. These rows were measured with the first
version of this pull request on main `b1d64c1c4` and were not repeated
after the rebase onto #10957.

| Task | Regraded | main b1d64c1c4 → first version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HumanEval+, MBPP+ | reference solutions | 159 → 163 of 164,
HumanEval/139 among the four; HumanEval/32's test rejects its float
answer both ways; 374 → 378 of 378 |
| GSM8K | chat replies to the zero-shot prompt, 9 runs, 11,871 rows | no
verdict moves in either filter |

Since #10957 the zero- and five-shot GSM8K tasks send chat prompts to
models that apply a chat template and completion prompts to the others.
We have no saved replies to the five-shot prompt, whose examples end in
a `#### ` line. Only 11 of the saved chat rows hold such a line, and
#10808's rules already reach flexible-extract on main, so that row does
not exercise the strict-match change; the unit cases do.

Grug's think markers need no scorer change here. With
`generation_extra_body: {"skip_special_tokens": false}`, which
`docs/references/evaluation-tasks.md` documents, a Grug checkpoint
served without a reasoning parser keeps its think markers, and the
MMLU-Pro and boxed-answer scorers cut the reasoning at the last one. On
saved zero-shot replies of five Grug-family checkpoints, keeping the
markers instead of deleting them adds 0.86 to 6.42 points on MMLU-Pro
and up to 0.67 on MATH500 and AIME24, the same at main `b1d64c1c4` and
on the first version of this branch. These replies do not cover the
canonical MMLU-Pro task, which sends up to five shots in one user
message: the review on #10828 measures Grug answering the examples
there, where the scorer reads the first `answer is (X)`. This branch
changes neither that prompt nor that rule.

Of the 236 corpora that the evaluation catalog builds for its 42
benchmarks, 71 get new recipe versions. 10 of them have a scorer change
that can move a grade: IFBench, CRUXEval, HumanEval+, MBPP+,
OlympiadBench twice and GSM8K four times (zero- and five-shot,
completion and chat), where only strict-match can move. The other 61
move only through hashes. 39, IFEval and MMLU-Pro among them, move
because every scorer revision hashes `grader.py`, which now lists
`relations.py`. The other 22 share a changed file: MATH500, AIME24,
AIME25, GSM8K chain-of-thought, the seven Minerva MATH subjects,
HumanEval zero-shot and ten-shot, and the three variants each of
TriviaQA, NQ-Open and DROP. The remaining 165 corpora keep their
versions. CI skips the IFBench cases: they need nltk, emoji, syllapy and
NLTK's punkt_tab data, which IFBench's grading environment installs and
the `taskcompendium-unit` lane does not.

This does not change entry points or the prompts and token caps that the
review on #10828 questions. The first version also added the missing
evidence pages to 11 FinanceBench rows, but that fix changed only files
under `vendor/evalchemy`, which #10957 deleted; the canonical task still
reads the old file at `623134de`. Still open in #10828: FinanceBench's
evidence pages, the two held default changes, and saved-response tests
and AIME25 coverage for Grug extraction.

commits.message:
[verifyit] Score malformed reasoning-gym replies as 0.0 (#11937)

Score 0.0 when a `reasoning-gym` scorer raises on a reply and accepts
the entry's own answer. The exception used to leave
`score_reasoning_gym_answer`, so the generated and Nemotron Ultra grade
scripts exited 1, the verifyit `reasoning-gym` mode wrote an
`infra_error` verdict, and training left the rollout out of the loss.
#11516 scored such a reply 0.0 for `prime_factorization` only. Six more
scorers of `reasoning-gym` 0.1.25 raise while they parse a reply:
`boxnet` (`TypeError` on a JSON number, `AttributeError` on a JSON
list), `game_of_life` (`KeyError` on `{}`), `coin_flip`,
`calendar_arithmetic` and `time_intervals` (`OverflowError` on `1e400`
or on 400 digits) and `propositional_logic` (`RecursionError` on 5,000
nested parentheses).

A raise can also come from a broken entry, which stays an error. After a
raise the scorer is called once more with the entry's own answer, and an
exception from that call propagates as before. `boxnet` and
`propositional_logic` entries have no answer (`null`), so for them a
raise on the reply scores 0.0 without that check. Only the exception
types that these scorers raised in the measurement below are caught:
`AttributeError`, `KeyError`, `OverflowError`, `RecursionError`,
`TypeError` and `ValueError`. #11516 caught `ValueError` for
`prime_factorization` only; it is now caught for every task.

I scored 87 fixed replies on the first 30 entries of each of the 104
generated tasks through the three grading paths. On main the six tasks
raise on 1,249 (task, entry, reply) cases in the verifyit mode, on 1,249
in the generated grade script and on 1,339 in the Nemotron Ultra script.
With this change none raises, and for every task and reply the mean
reward and the share of entries with reward 1.0 are the same as on main
when a raise counts as 0. Run end to end with one such reply per task,
both grade scripts exit 1 on main and print 0.0 here.

Fixes #11652

[verifyit] Honor explicit positivity in scalar grading (#11930)

Scalar math contracts can declare positive symbols. When ordinary
math-verify comparison fails, the grader substitutes those assumptions
into both parsed expressions and accepts only if their difference
simplifies exactly to zero. Contracts without assumptions retain their
existing grading policy.

The pinned HARDMath `poly1_train` symbolic nondimensionalization
questions omit the positive coefficient domain described in #11740.
Their converted prompts now state it, and their scalar contracts compare
the right side of the epsilon equation. Through the converted tasks, all
89 regrouped answers and all 89 source replies score 1; all 89
wrong-exponent controls score 0. The other 12 symbolic source replies
still score 1.

The direct grader and converter suites passed (227 tests), and the
Pyrefly baseline passed. The broader affected-test run reached its
600-second cap after 1,734 passes; five evaluation task-driver tests
failed during local `bwrap` setup. The same setup failure reproduced in
a clean `main` worktree.

Fixes #11740

[eval] Accept Kyiv in IFBench European capitals check (#11926)

The IFBench European-capitals checker now accepts the complete 28-city
latitude order, with Kyiv between Brussels and Prague. The complete
answer previously scored 0 and the 27-city list without Kyiv scored 1;
those grades are now reversed. Wrong-order and wrong-set lists still
score 0 in strict and loose grading.

The checker is copied from Marin `623134de` (Apache-2.0). Newly prepared
canonical IFBench corpora pick up the correction through the scorer
content hash. The existing Micro210 policy remains pinned to the old
`runtime-v4` evalchemy wheel; a new runtime and policy revision are
still needed before Micro210 grades change. #10423 did not change this
checker.

The regression failed on both reported answers before the edit, then all
four cases passed with IFBench's pinned checker packages. The
instruction test file passed all six cases.

Part of #11828.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[iris] Remove the Iris-owned sandbox RuntimeClass on CoreWeave (#11841)

CoreWeave has deprecated its gVisor runtime handlers. SANDBOX pods on
CoreWeave will move to its managed `cw-kata-qemu` RuntimeClass on a
dedicated CPU node pool once CoreWeave enables it. This prepares Iris
for that move without changing any running cluster.

- Remove the Iris-owned sandbox RuntimeClass that #11345 added for
cw-us-east-02a (`iris-gvisor-cpu`, created by Pulumi): the Pulumi code
path, the `provisioning.coreweave.sandbox_runtime` config subtree, and
the rollout docs. The 02a config goes back to CoreWeave's `gvisor`
class, which the other CoreWeave clusters use by default. The deploy
preflight marks a missing RuntimeClass as CoreWeave-provided.
- Describe the SANDBOX runtime per backend in docs, proto comments, CLI
help and error messages, which said gVisor everywhere. Identifiers such
as `--image-backend gvisor` are unchanged.

Rendered cluster configs differ from main only on 02a (class name,
dropped subtree), and pod manifests are identical. Main fails the deploy
preflight on 02a because `iris-gvisor-cpu` was never created there; this
branch passes it on all four CoreWeave clusters. `pulumi preview` on the
four stacks differs from main only on 02a, which no longer plans to
create that class.

The pod placement for the Kata pool is left to the change that
provisions the pool and its Kueue flavor.

Part of #11343

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
Keep logging on the live stderr across stream swaps (#11895)

pytest and Click's CliRunner capture output by swapping sys.stderr and
closing the previous stream. configure_logging bound
StreamHandler(sys.stderr) once, so after the first captured invocation
every later log record failed with "ValueError: I/O operation on closed
file" and logging printed a "--- Logging error ---" traceback into the
next captured output. In CI this corrupted the snowball YAML status that
test_rl parses (the unit (marin 3/4) failures on #11853).

LiveStderrHandler resolves sys.stderr per record, so records always
reach the live stderr. The snowball status parser reads result.stdout
now: the status document is stdout content and stderr lines must not
enter the parse. A rigging regression test reproduces the closed-stream
swap; the failure mode itself was reproduced in a Linux container
(handler bound inside one CliRunner isolation, warning during a second
invoke) where the dump appears in the captured output before the fix and
the record appears after it.

---------

Co-authored-by: penfeuer <penfeuer@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: davidlundgren
commits.message:
[tests] Parse the migration CLI summary from stdout (#11912)

`test_migration_cli_reads_archived_legacy_shards` failed on `main`
(marin shard 4 at `eecb397a0c`) when parsing the migration CLI's JSON
summary. The test read the last line of `CliRunner`'s `output`, which
interleaves stderr log records with stdout; on main a `validated ...`
log line followed the summary. The test now parses the last line of
`result.stdout`.

The identity repins this PR first carried landed separately in #11898.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[eval] Read Micro210 policy inputs from Hugging Face (#11904)

Read the Micro210 policy and prepared-task inputs from content-pinned
Hugging Face
repositories instead of private GCS, so evaluation startup does not need
GCP
credentials on CoreWeave.

The policy JSON is public content: `open-athena/micro210-policy` holds
one commit per
policy version, tagged `2026.11.18` and `2026.11.20-together`, and the
code pins the
repository, commit revision, byte size and SHA-256 with the existing
verify-on-read
check. Bytes are unchanged (SHA-256 `8f7ef817…`, 121292 bytes; legacy
`e0faa32c…`,
122243 bytes). The prepared-task parquet re-hosts GPQA-Diamond, AIME,
OlympiadBench and
SWE-bench items, so it moved to the private
`open-athena/micro210-prepared-tasks`
repository and CoreWeave tasks read it with the standard HF_TOKEN. Its
bytes are also
unchanged (SHA-256 `ba099cbc…`, 17152253 bytes, 440 rows) and the
adoption version is
`2026.11.20.1`, so a cached GCS source cannot replace the new one.
`scripts/ops/upload_micro210_policy_hf.py` publishes both repositories
and is
idempotent: versions whose tag already carries the pinned bytes are
verified and
skipped.

A CPU-only `cw-us-east-08a` task with no GCP credentials ran the
publishing script,
read every pinned `hf://` reference back through the new code path,
verified the
digests and the 440-row count, and confirmed the public policy is
anonymously readable
while the private repository rejects anonymous reads (HTTP 401). Dataset
cards link
#10804 and contain no names, emails, or usernames. No evaluation was
run.

Fixes #11834

---------

Co-authored-by: penfeuer <penfeuer@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
Re-pin the levanter trainer-config fingerprints (#11898)

#10969 (518877698a) added the file_io_locking field to
TensorStoreWriteConfig. That field is part of every levanter trainer
config, so the step fingerprints covering trainer configs changed and
two pin tests fail on main.

Re-pin the shifted values: the iceball-micro evaluation fingerprint
(5fc130f9 to a0268301) and the eight SFT recipe fingerprints that carry
trainer configs. The hf-to-levanter conversion and the mochi HF export
carry no trainer config and keep their pins.

The new values come from that config change alone. Both tests pass at
20f92312db, the commit before #10969, fail from 518877698a onward, and
the computed fingerprints are identical at 518877698a, 0b5f84ec12, and
this branch's base eecb397a0c.

Co-authored-by: penfeuer <penfeuer@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[shellbox] Keep Daytona commands across a lost connection (#11796)

A Daytona machine now finishes a command whose provider request failed
in transit: the request lost its connection or got a 502, 503, or 504
status. Before, a `DaytonaConnectionError` from any request of
`Machine.run` failed the command, and the SkyRL task worker masked the
rollout with the model turns it already had. In a Quick RL Loop run of
1536 rollouts on forge tasks, resets during a model command and during
grading caused 2 of the 7 masked rollouts.

One `Machine.run` sends several provider requests. The requests that
prepare the command directory, upload stdin and the script, measure and
download the output, and remove the files give the same result when they
run twice, so the machine repeats them up to three times with backoff.
`Machine.upload` and `Machine.download` restart as a whole. Sandbox
deletion and snapshot reads use the same check and retry, which now live
in `backends/daytona/transient.py`.

The request that runs the command is not repeatable, because the
provider can start the command before the request fails. The command
script now claims its private directory before it runs, so a repeated
request starts the command only if the first request did not. If the
repeated request started the command, its response is the result.
Otherwise the machine reads the exit code that the exit trap records,
until the command's timeout. A command shell that was killed records no
exit code; the machine detects the dead process and raises instead of
waiting. The rollout keeps its turns and its machine. A failure that
persists still raises the provider error, and the worker masks the
rollout as before.

The task worker also names the cause of every `TaskMachineError` in its
warning, redacted. It named only Daytona errors, so a third masked
rollout in that run had no cause in the log. That change has no test.

The new tests use the local sandbox fake, which runs on Linux only. One
check ran against the Daytona service: the client closed the connection
of a command request 4 seconds into a 15-second command. The command ran
once and `Machine.run` returned its exit code and output after 18.6
seconds. A client-side close stands in for the provider-side reset,
which the check could not produce.

#11586 moves `Machine.run` to polled provider sessions and conflicts
with this change in `machine.py`. Its status polls are repeatable, so it
replaces the exit-code file; the claim directory can make its command
submission repeatable. #11762 restarts a rollout that loses its
connection at machine start and edits other lines of `task_worker.py`.

Fixes #11795

---------

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <ravwojdyla@gmail.com>
